headline: Army Corps Transforms Harbor Mud Into Thriving Bird Island
meta_description: In Savannah, Georgia, dredged harbor mud became an 8-acre island that attracted over 300 bird nests in its first season.
summary_short: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers turned 160,000 cubic yards of dredged mud into a productive bird sanctuary in Savannah.
body:
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in Savannah, Georgia, found an elegant solution to harbor maintenance: transform dredged mud into habitat. The result was an 8-acre bird island that welcomed more than 300 nests during its first nesting season.

When maintenance dredging produces 160,000 cubic yards of mud, disposal typically means hauling it away. Instead, engineers reshaped the material into a new island. The gamble paid off almost immediately—birds recognized the newly created space as suitable nesting ground, arriving and settling without delay.

The project demonstrates how infrastructure work can serve dual purposes: keeping shipping channels navigable while restoring habitat for wildlife. One dredging project became a sanctuary, turning what might have been waste into something alive with possibility.
quick_facts: 160,000 cubic yards of dredged harbor mud repurposed
8-acre bird island created in Savannah, Georgia
300+ nests built in the island's first nesting season
U.S. Army Corps of Engineers executed the project
